question.text: Ms. Priya Shah, Managing Partner of 'Arya Buyout Partners', is explaining to her IC why a buyout is structurally different from a plain-vanilla private equity investment. Which of the following is the ESSENTIAL distinction?

answer.text: A buyout targets primary share issuance for growth capital, while PE targets secondary shares
A buyout involves only debt financing while PE involves only equity financing
A buyout is restricted to listed companies while PE is restricted to unlisted companies
A buyout seeks control via secondary shares, while PE subscribes to primary shares for growth capital

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 8.3 explicitly distinguishes: PE subscribes to PRIMARY shares (financing the company, minority, no control), whereas a buyout acquires SECONDARY shares from existing controlling shareholders to obtain control (usually 51%+). The Trap: Option A inverts primary/secondary. Option C is false — buyouts include both listed (take-private) and unlisted targets. Option D confuses LBO financing mix with the definition of buyout. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C is unique in testing buyout structuring mechanics; XIX-A/B and IX (Mergers & Acquisitions) touch on takeover code but do not test the PE-vs-buyout primary/secondary contrast. Manager's Pro-Tip: When launching a buyout-focused Cat II AIF, model the capital required for 51%+ stake upfront — a PE-style 10-15% ticket will not close a control deal and investors will be disappointed at year 3.
